title: InputGroup
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField leadingIcon and trailingIcon slots, through MonarchTextField
summary: A recipe, not a component: text, a unit or a button attached to a MonarchTextField through its leading and trailing slots.
whenToUse: For a field with a fixed prefix or unit (https://, a currency sign, kg) or an action that belongs to the field (copy, show, search).
whenNotToUse: For a password use MonarchPasswordInput, for a number with steps MonarchNumberInput. For actions about the whole form put MonarchButtons under the fields.
api: MonarchTextField(value, onValueChange, label = …, leadingIcon = { MonarchText(prefix) }, trailingIcon = { MonarchButton(…, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm) })

options.name: leadingIcon
options.description: Text or an icon attached at the start of the field, such as https:// or a currency sign.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: Text, a unit or a ghost MonarchButton attached at the end of the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Set enabled = false on MonarchTextField and on the attached button.

states.name: error
states.description: Set errorText on MonarchTextField: the outline, the attached text and the message take the danger color.

appearance: One outlined field: the attached text uses the muted color of the field's icons and the attached button the ghost variant, all inside the field's input border and focus ring. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's InputGroup, InputGroupAddon and InputGroupButton are three components around an Input; on Android they are the leading and trailing slots of MonarchTextField, which mirror in right-to-left layouts without an align option. The parity plan names prefix and suffix slots: the Material 3 OutlinedTextField has prefix and suffix, but MonarchTextField does not expose them yet, so the recipe uses the icon slots; text in the leading slot is always shown, while a Material prefix only shows once the field has focus or text. The web's sizes are not offered. iOS composes the same recipe from TextField and MonarchButton in an HStack.
accessibility: The field keeps its label; attached text is read by TalkBack as part of the field, before or after the value.
An attached MonarchButton is its own element with its own name and a 48dp touch target.
The field is at least 48dp high.
edgeCases: A long prefix takes width from the text; keep attached text short.
At font scale 2.0 the attached text grows with the field's text.

examples.title: URL prefix in a Field
examples.template:
MonarchTextField(
    value = address,
    onValueChange = { address = it },
    label = {{label}},
    placeholder = {{placeholder}},
    helperText = {{description}},
    leadingIcon = { MonarchText(text = {{prefix}}, color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted) },
)
examples.code:
MonarchTextField(
    value = address,
    onValueChange = { address = it },
    label = "Website",
    placeholder = "example.com",
    helperText = "Without the protocol.",
    leadingIcon = { MonarchText(text = "https://", color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted) },
)

examples.title: A unit after the number
examples.code:
MonarchTextField(
    value = weight,
    onValueChange = { weight = it },
    label = "Weight",
    trailingIcon = { MonarchText(text = "kg") },
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Decimal),
)
